failures: src/contextlens/cards/dataset.py _long_turns/_check_train_scenarios: the held-out guard matches whole turns exactly after lowercasing and whitespace normalisation, so a light paraphrase of a dev/test conversation (one word altered in each turn, a prefix added, a word swapped) passes with 0% turn overlap. Reproduce: python tmp-T6.1/leak.py from the worktree (PYTHONPATH=src): variants oneword, twoword, synonym, prefix print 'PASSED (not refused)'. The decision says dev gold must not leak into training; the set is written by T5.2 with a model that may have seen dev scenarios, which is exactly where light paraphrase arises. Fix: compare with fuzzy per-turn similarity (for example word 3-gram shingle Jaccard or difflib ratio over turns, and also check gold answer/question text against the dev ones), refuse above a threshold, and add a test with a one-word-edited copy.
notes: Gaps for T6.2 (not failures): (1) consistent-labelled scenarios yield no card (dropped_no_card_for_label count); they need a card design or are lost to training. (2) train() loads only the QMSum examples (load_examples('train') without include_scenarios), so T6.2 must pass include_scenarios and call build_examples with train_scenarios and abstain_cap=0.25, fixed seed; the real train-and-VRAM check (the real-marked test, GPU, Qwen download) was not run here and belongs to T6.2. (3) The real set yields 226 examples (150 train) with 65% abstained because 569 answered candidates exceed MAX_GOLD=4 and are dropped; the 25% cap on QMSum alone would leave about 78 answered plus 26 abstained, so T6.2's under-300 notice to the coordinator is likely to fire. (4) requests ConnectionError falls back to Qwen3-4B (it would fail again there, so low harm). (5) If PEFT attach fails after the primary loads, the first model may still hold GPU memory, which inflates the later peak reading (conservative). (6) Two untested rules listed above (text-copy exclusion, recent window before the first gold turn). No QMSum text was copied into this file.
